name: hybrid_directory_planning
scope_warning: LAYOUT AND COST MODEL ONLY. No circuit exists for the hybrid; the two halves' circuits exist separately and have never been run together. Every figure is a modelled product count on the same model used for the dense baseline, so the RATIOS are internally consistent, but none is a measured byte count. The primary-type map used here is derived from edge counts, which is a sizing convenience and NOT a deployment path -- a deployment must take it from a published ontology or the block widths leak the owners' edge distribution.
headline_finding: Neither candidate layout wins alone. Routing the 54.1% of edges whose relation domain matches the entity's primary type through an affine type-blocked half, and the 45.9% residual through a hashed half, models 92x against the dense folded directory at FULL edge coverage -- 1.80x better than hashed-alone sized the same safe way.

why_a_hybrid.type_blocked_alone: Affine addressing needs a partition, one type per entity. A Freebase entity carries 1 to 189 domains, so forcing a partition drops 45.9% of edges. 186x, but only 54% coverage.
why_a_hybrid.hashed_alone: Needs no contiguity, so it keeps every edge, but pays a key-tag comparison on every fetched slot. 51x at full coverage with leakage-safe capacity.
why_a_hybrid.the_composition: A key's half is publicly derivable from (entity, relation) and the ontology, so a lookup reads both halves and sums -- at most one contributes, and no secret branch is needed. The hashed half then carries roughly half the keys, so its comparison is paid on half as many.

modelled_products_per_query.reading: The two halves come out nearly equal (7.7M vs 9.0M), which is the signature of a well-placed split: neither dominates, so moving keys either way would cost more than it saves.

comparison.note: All rows model the same query shape (1 + 15 addresses) on the full WebQSP graph. The dense baseline is the FOLDED circuit, which is the honest reference.

the_comparison_was_made_fair.issue: An earlier hashed-alone figure of 50x used capacity sized to the MEASURED worst-case bucket load, which LEAKAGE_ABUSE.md section 8 records as a data-dependent public parameter and therefore not deployable.
the_comparison_was_made_fair.resolution: Re-derived with public_capacity_bound on the full key set: 51x rather than 53x, so the safe bound costs only 1.04x here. The hybrid's 92x uses the safe bound throughout, so the 1.80x advantage over hashed-alone is like-for-like and not an artifact of comparing safe against unsafe sizing.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: NOT an MPC result. No hybrid circuit exists; no bytes, rounds or seconds measured.
NOT a validated cost model. The 50-product equality constant is an estimate; it is applied identically to both sides of every ratio, but absolute figures are uncalibrated.

NOT a leakage-free split as measured. The primary-type map here comes from edge counts, which is owner data. A deployment needs the map from a published ontology; the split's 54.1/45.9 ratio would then differ.
NOT practical. 16.8M products per query is 92x better and still far above any usable per-query cost. This narrows five orders of magnitude to roughly three.

NOT a coverage claim about retrieval quality. 'Full edge coverage' means every edge has a home in one of the two halves; it says nothing about the separate losses from the fanout bound and top-k, which rag_quality_at_scale.json measures at 2.0 points on MetaQA and webqsp_smoke.json at 9.09 on WebQSP.
